info.title: Aleth Engine
info.summary: The local AI execution engine: plan, gate, execute -- on one loopback port.
info.description: The whole HTTP surface of the engine: the typed operation table (`api.operations.OPERATIONS`) plus the gateway's own infrastructure reads and event streams (`api.gateway.ROUTES`). One process, one port. Every request body is a strict model (`extra="forbid"`) and every operation answer is the shared envelope; every non-2xx body is `ErrorResponse`. The server binds 127.0.0.1 and refuses any peer that is not loopback.

servers.description: The engine's single socket (ALETH_API_PORT overrides the port).

tags.name: operations
tags.description: The typed capability surface: every engine action the UI may invoke, and nothing else.

tags.name: infrastructure

get.summary: The engine's event bus, as a server-sent event stream.
get.description: Frames of JSON events on the bus natively bound to the window and the console. Never terminates voluntarily: a heartbeat comment frame keeps the connection warm.

get.summary: Liveness and posture: the engine's own view of itself.
The same stream, narrowed to one run.
get.description: A `stream`, not an `operation`: it does not answer once. The frames are the hub's, filtered to the named intent, so a client sees exactly the run it asked about.

OperationOk.description: The envelope. `ok: true` carries the service payload in `data`; `ok: false` carries the reason in `error`.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request: the body did not validate against the strict model.

Forbidden.description: Not loopback, or the engine is draining. The socket's only boundary.

Conflict.description: Conflict: another merge holds the workspace write lock.

InternalError.description: The operation failed, or its answer broke the envelope contract.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The engine service is not attached to the gateway yet.

AcknowledgeRequest.description: Acknowledge a failed intent, or every unacknowledged one when no id is given.

AcknowledgeResponse.description: How many failures the user's acknowledgement cleared.

ErrorResponse.description: Every non-2xx body has this shape, so the frontend has one failure branch.

HealthResponse.description: What the gateway will say about itself.

IntentIdRequest.description: An operation that names one intent and nothing else. A GET carries it in the query.

IntentLedgerEntry.description: One row of the durable intent ledger.

IntentQueueStatus.description:
The queue's own state, plus the ledger that outlives it.

The queue is in memory and dies with the process; the ledger is what a restart reconciles
against. ``pending_failure`` is the gate the UI reads: while it is set, the user has not yet
been told that their last run did not do what they asked.

IntentRequest.description:
One execution signal from the UI.

``message`` is the directive text; ``action_type`` names the branch; ``action_params`` carries
the branch's own arguments (a target task id, an artifact key). Nothing here is trusted to
execute anything -- it is a *request*, and the queue is where it waits for the orchestrator.

``validate_default`` is load-bearing: without it the blank-prompt check below only fires when a
caller *spells out* ``"message": ""``, and an omitted message sails through as the default --
the check has to be a property of the request, not of how the JSON was written.

IntentView.description: One intent as the queue reports it.

InterruptRequest.description: Hold a running intent for the user (Phase 33).

MetricsView.description: The progress counters, exactly as the engine computes them.

OperationEnvelope.description:
The one answer shape for the typed operation surface (``api.operations``).

``data`` carries the service's own payload -- the dictionaries the UI and the
characterization suite already speak -- so moving the transport did not invent a second wire
format for the plan. The envelope is what makes a single client-side failure branch possible.

PlanListResponse.description: Which plans exist: what the store holds and what the workspace has on disk.

PlanView.description: The active plan: its tasks, in document order, and its counters.

ResumeRequest.description:
Release a paused intent, carrying the user's correction.

``correction`` is what makes this the steering wheel rather than a resume button: it is injected
into the run's context window as a ``[user]`` message before the loop continues.

RollbackRequest.description:
Rewind a held run to ``step`` (Phase 35).

The step is the run's own step number, not an index into a UI list: it is what the shadow's
snapshot tags and the per-step ledger rows are keyed on, so the files, the context window and
the bill all resolve to the same point.

ServiceRefusal.description:
The only shape in which a service may report a failure.

The client's type guard keys on ``success is False``: that is what it turns into a thrown
``ApiError``. A payload that carries an ``error`` without that flag is therefore delivered as
a *successful* answer and read as one -- the failure is swallowed, and the caller carries on
with state the backend just said was bad. The gateway validates every answer against this
model (``api.gateway``), so the anomaly cannot be reintroduced by a future method.

``extra`` is allowed on purpose: a refusal carries its own context -- a ``task_id``, an empty
``variables`` list, the payload keys the caller was expecting -- and that shape differs per
operation. What is *not* optional is the flag and the reason.

TaskView.description:
One task's status and scheduling surface, and nothing else.

Deliberately not the whole node: the DAG carries fields the UI has no use for, and a wire
contract that mirrors an internal model is one that changes whenever the model does.

TelemetryListResponse.description: The newest receipts, bounded, with the ledger's own total for context.

TelemetryReceiptView.description: One append-only ledger row, as written by the exec server.

WorkspaceMergeRequest.description:
Apply the shadow, or (``approve=False``) discard it and leave the host untouched.

``intent_id`` is required for the same reason as the diff: a merge that cannot name the run
that produced the changes would have to guess, and guessing is how the wrong changes land.

WorkspaceStagingRequest.description:
Which shadow to read the delta of. The intent id is required: a shadow maps 1:1 to an
execution, so a request that cannot name one is a request the engine must refuse.
